column12: Judgement on the comparator. Vyvgart Hytrulo is the only non-immunoglobulin biologic labelled for CIDP in the US, and it is argenx's own, so argenx would price a second CIDP biologic against it. Empasiprubart is an IV infusion every 4 weeks, so it is physician-administered and billed under Part B, which fits a Part B anchor. Case for higher: CMS 2024 beneficiaries mix gMG with partial-year CIDP starts after the June 2024 launch. Vyvgart IV reads $231,053 per Part B beneficiary in 2024, but it is labelled for gMG only in the US. Hytrulo's own Part D reads $191,644. Case for lower: EMVIGORATE's comparator is IVIg itself, and the book carries no CIDP-labelled immunoglobulin brand to price it from (only Octagam, $26,251 per Part B beneficiary across all its uses)

column11: Social Security Act section 1847A: Medicare Part B pays 106% of ASP, and ASP is already net of manufacturer discounts and rebates, so 1 - 1/1.06 = 0.056604 (backend/gross_to_net.py house rule for a Part B anchor; the riliprubart and frexalimab seeds use it)

Empasiprubart's two Phase 3s, EMVIGORATE (NCT06920004, adults on stable maintenance IVIg) and EMNERGIZE (NCT07091630, adults treatment-naive or off prior therapy with residual disability), together span the same adult CIDP population, so its label would reach the same pool: 77,058 x 1.0
column12: Judgement: the label is taken to read 'adults with CIDP', as Hytrulo's does, which the researcher also expected. It is set to the pool the book already reads Hytrulo's label as reaching, so both drugs are measured over one denominator and the peak below is the book's single Hytrulo rate. The riliprubart seed's 0.2643 (IVIg subset, 20,367) nests inside it. Case for lower: the researcher's 0.5386, the 41,505 of 77,058 with a CIDP-listed treatment claim in 2023 (Gable Table 2), as a stand-in for disease that needs therapy. argenx's Q2 2026 deck (6-K 0001697862-26-000033, exhibit 3) supports a similar split: 42K diagnosed, 24K treated, 18K not treated. That filter only holds if Hytrulo's rate is also re-based over the same 41,505, to 5.17% against the 2.78% the riliprubart seed carries for the same launch. Gable's 'treated' also means any claim for a listed drug in 2023, and 29,009 of the 41,505 are steroid claims in a cohort where 47% have diabetes and 44% COPD, so it is not a clean CIDP severity filter. Not applied: adults only (Gable includes children, and the riliprubart seed's Hytrulo rate is over the same all-age pool)

column11: The book's Vyvgart Hytrulo CIDP launch rate, as the riliprubart seed carries it (lookup.py seed Riliprubart): argenx AAN 2025 release (argenx.com/news/2024/argenx-highlights-vyvgart-data-at-aan-2025-setting-new-standard): 1,316 CIDP patients treated with Vyvgart Hytrulo as of 2025-01-31, 224 days after the 2024-06-21 FDA approval. 1,316 x 365/224 = 2,144 a year, over Hytrulo's label pool, the 77,058 US CIDP patients of Gable 2026 = 2.78%
column12: 1.0 multiple on Hytrulo, a judgement. On the whole pool this is 0.0278 x 77,058 = 2,142 new starts a year from the opening pool at peak, Hytrulo's measured rate. On the engine's convention, which adds incidence to the base, the rate is 2,144 / (77,058 + 9,238) = 2.48%. Case for higher: dosing every 4 weeks, a head-to-head design against IVIg, argenx's CIDP sales force already in place, and a non-FcRn mechanism for the third of patients who fail FcRn (ADHERE stage A: 108 of 322 without confirmed improvement, PubMed 39304241); launch-period rates also understate peak. Case for lower: argenx's second CIDP biologic would take patients from its own Hytrulo; IV infusion against self-injection; riliprubart (Sanofi) may compete in the IVIg-maintained segment at the same time. The 1,316 release does not say US only
